scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) in the existing harness. Owner replica 0 proposes command X with a real defs.GPropose attached (command id 77, reply writer over a local buffer); replica 1 holds a conflicting command so its pre-accept reply is non-equal, and replica 1 fails after replying; replica 3, which holds no command, recovers instance (0,0) while the owner is still alive; the quiescent exchange is completed; the owner's propose channel is then drained and its instance state, pending proposals and reply writer size are recorded. After the replacement decision and the observed re-queue, the harness calls handlePropose with the re-queued proposal (creating instance (0,1)), delivers that instance's pre-accept replies, and invokes the package's own execution entry point for it, recording the execution result, the reply writer size and the decoded reply.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
The owner stays alive throughout, modelling a slow but reachable owner whose instance is decided by another replica's recovery.
No executor goroutine runs, so any reply observed would have to come from the recovery/handleCommit paths rather than from the state-machine execution path.
The execution entry point is invoked directly, as the package's executeCommands goroutine would, because the harness runs no run() loop.
excluded: No run() loop, no executeCommands goroutine and no client socket; the client request is supplied as the target's own defs.GPropose value.

basis.prefix: The harness attaches a real GPropose to the owner's startPhase1 call, drives the conflicting premise and the owner's non-equal pre-accept reply, fails replica 1, calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at replica 3, delivers the emitted Prepare/PrepareReply/PreAccept traffic and the resulting Commit through the target's handlers, and finally drains the owner's ProposeChan while recording the owner's instance status, committed command, remaining pending proposals and reply buffer size. Then the re-queued proposal is passed to the replica's own handlePropose, its pre-accept exchange is delivered, and Exec.executeCommand is called for instance (0,1); the reply written for command id 77 is decoded from the proposal's reply writer.
basis.requirement: A committed replacement decision for an instance must not silently consume the client request the owner had pending for it: the pending proposal must be re-offered for a new decision, and the client must not be told the original request completed. The re-queued proposal must also be able to complete: after it is decided, the target's execution path must deliver a reply for the same command id.
basis.responsibility: The owner's own commit handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082-1100) and the recovery that produced the replacement decision (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313); the client request was admitted through the replica's own propose path.

comparisons.description: The owner's pending client request is re-queued exactly once after its instance was decided with the replacement NOOP; violated when no proposal arrives on the owner's propose channel.

After the re-queued request is decided again at instance (0,1), the target's execution path produces a client reply carrying the same command id (77); violated when no reply is written or it carries a different command id. Admitted on the re-proposed instance's decided state, which shares the identity of the reply observation.
